newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Two weeks after his 100th Test appearance, Rugby Union player David Campese has been dumped from the Wallaby side to play Scotland in Edinburgh on Saturday. The 34-year-old player has confirmed he will end his 15-year career with the tour to Italy, Britain and Ireland. Page 44.

Two of Australia's best batsmen, Ricky Ponting and Michael Bevan, are expected to play each other next week for one position in the Test team. Both players are expected to be chosen for the Australian XI team in the final lead up match with the West Indies before the first Test in Brisbane the following week. Both Bevan and Ponting played in the only Test against India, which Australia lost by seven wickets. Page 44.

A mystery benefactor, believed to be Kerry Packer, funded a A$3 million rescue package to keep the South Queensland Crushers in next year's Australian Rugby League competition. Administrators KPMG are to settle the conditions of the Deed Of Company agreement and expect full control to return to the new board members before Christmas. Page 43.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Melbourne Cup winner Saintly is being prepared for his next challenge against a world-class field in the Japan Cup. The horse is to leave Australia next week as the country's only representative in the event to be held in Tokyo on November 24. Page 48.

The International Sailing Federation yesterday ignored concerns about unsuitable conditions and boat traffic to announce Sydney Harbour as its chief location for the Sydney 2000. The ISAF have decided four of the five courses will be based inside the harbour, Rushcutters Bay will be the onshore headquarters for the Olympics and a National Sailing Academy is to be established at the Rushcutters for use after the Olympics. Page 48.

The Wallabies stretched their unbeaten European tour record to five matches when they overwhelmed Scottish Districts 25-9 in Tuesday's match. The match saw the injury of yet another player, Adam Magro, who is awaiting confirmation from x-rays after he left the arena with a suspected broken left foot. Page 48.
THE AGE

Australia's number one golfer Greg Norman is expected to consult swing guru David Leadbetter in an effort to win a major championship in the U.S. before retiring. Greg Norman confirmed the split with his old coach Butch Harmon yesterday and said he will re-evaluate his playing future after 2000. Page C20.

Whilst Bart Cummings, the winner of the Melbourne Cup and nine Cups previously, was doing the rounds of interviews on his latest success with horse Saintly, the master trainer claimed he still had his mind on the next job at hand, adding another VC Oaks at Flemington to his collection. Cummings first won the Oaks in 1964 with his filly Light Fingers, the same horse who also gave him his first Melbourne Cup the following year. Page C20.

Glenn McGrath and Mark Waugh have pulled out of the New South Wales side to play Victoria in the Sheffield Shield match starting tomorrow at the Sydney Cricket Ground, citing injuries. Waugh has come back from the Indian tour nursing a calf strain and McGrath has severe blistering on his heel. NSW Coach Geoff Lawson said the loss of the two was a blow for the side, but he couldn't complain with others like Michael Bevan, Mark Taylor and Steve Waugh still on side. Page C19.
HERALD SUN

David Boon may be considered for an unexpected recall to international cricket if Australia cannot find a suitable replacement for him early in the summer. Boon, 35, retired from the game last summer but is reported to have given Australian chairman of electors, Trevor Johns, licence to approach him as an emergency option against the West Indies this season. Page 104.

Australian golf champion Karrie Webb met with the country's number one, Greg Norman, at the Yarra Yarra Golf Club yesterday. Webb spent most of the afternoon speaking to Norman on how to handle the increasing off-field pressures that accompany success on the greens. Norman will return to the U.S. before playing in the Australian Open in two weeks while Webb hopes to continue her form in the Australian Women's Open which starts today. Page 104.

World renowned jockey Pat Eddery believes Melbourne Cup winner Saintly is the horse to give Australia its second win in the A$5 million Japan Cup, due to be run in Tokyo on November 24. Eddery believes the acceleration the gelding showed in the last leg of the 3200 metre race is the key ingredient required to win in Japan. Page 104.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Former New South Wales Rugby Union boss Ken Elphick has been accused of organising cash payment for the whole New Zealand team to play games in Sydney during the 1980s. The evidence was revealed in Elphick's District Court trial on charges of defrauding he NSW Rugby Union of A$851,000. Page 80.

The Canberra Raiders rugby league team is preparing to begin competing in next year's Super League without international full-back Brett Mullins who is still recovering from shoulder reconstruction surgery two weeks ago and is not expected to be fully fit until March 1997. The remaining Super League draw will not be announced until later this month, but is expected to begin in February or March. Page 79.

Retired Australian cricketer David Boon has given consent to be approached as an emergency replacement for the West Indies Test team this season if Australia cannot find a suitable replacement for him early in the summer. The 35-year-old retired last summer but if Boon is in form the 107-Test veteran will remain an option for the panel. Page 78.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
